reproduce.title: Measure auto-hide reveal/collapse at shared taskbar edges
prerequisites: Isolated interactive Windows test setup with Command Palette dock and taskbar; disposable dock settings and a second layout/scaling control when available.
steps: 1. Hold the cursor stationary over the bottom taskbar inside the dock horizontal span; record whether reveal/collapse repeats.
2. Record cursor coordinates, revealed/collapsed rectangles and each state transition, then move deliberately toward/away from the edge.
3. Repeat dock/taskbar same-edge versus different-edge layouts and supported top/left/right dock placements; record scaling and monitor offsets.
4. Validate a candidate region policy against the state trace: stationary overlap must not oscillate, intentional edge activation and normal collapse must still work.
reproduce.expected_result: A stable state for a stationary taskbar pointer and reliable deliberate reveal/collapse across supported edges. Choose a region policy from the proven transition, not an untested bottom-only clamp.
setup: Start with bottom dock plus bottom taskbar and auto-hide enabled. Record taskbar auto-hide mode and monitor work area without changing the reporter configuration.
